turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from device physics

Scanning the training set, the highest‑efficiency configurations cluster very tightly around a few recognizable "winning recipes":

**Regular (n‑i‑p) champion recipe:** mixed A‑cation, mixed‑halide perovskite (FAMAPbBrI / CsFAMAPbBrI) + SnO2 or TiO2‑c|TiO2‑mp ETL + Spiro‑MeOTAD HTL + Au back contact, made by simple spin‑coating (or double spin‑coating). Small additives at the ETL/perovskite or HTL/metal interface (SrCl2, trimethylamine‑oxide, CH3O‑PEIA, C9, ImAcHcl) push the champions above 20% by passivating traps and improving band alignment/selectivity at the ETL interface without adding parasitic resistance. This is the dominant cluster (17–22.9%).

**Inverted (p‑i‑n) champion recipe:** CsFAMAPbBrI with a fullerene‑bilayer ETL (C60 or PCBM‑60, capped with BCP for good electron selectivity/blocking of holes) + PTAA HTL (deeper HOMO than PEDOT:PSS, giving better Voc and less non‑radiative recombination at the HTL interface) + Cu or Ag contact. These recipes reach 18–20.3%, clearly outperforming PEDOT:PSS‑based pin cells (typically <15%) because PTAA gives superior interface selectivity and reduced recombination.

Applying these criteria to the pool:

- **c085** – CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, C60|BCP ETL, PTAA (+PFN‑Br interfacial passivation) HTL, Cu contact — matches the best p‑i‑n template (20.1–20.3% analogs) with an added passivation layer that should further reduce interfacial recombination.
- **c093** – CsFAMAPbBrI, pin, PCBM‑60|BCP ETL, PTAA HTL, Ag contact — near‑identical to the 20.295% training entry, differing only in ETL layer choice/back contact, still highly selective fullerene/BCP + PTAA stack.
- **c047** – FAMAPbBrI, nip, SnO2‑c ETL, Spiro‑MeOTAD HTL, Au contact — this exact ETL/HTL/contact combination recurs repeatedly among the 17.8–20.5% champions, indicating a robust, well‑passivated SnO2/perovskite interface.
- **c091** – FAMAPbBrI, nip, TiO2‑c|TiO2‑mp ETL, Spiro‑MeOTAD + NaYF4 HTL additive, Au contact — mirrors the SrCl2‑modified 20.81% champion; the NaYF4 additive likely serves a similar passivation/light‑management role.
- **c059** – CsFAMAPbBrI, nip, SnO2‑QDs ETL, Spiro‑MeOTAD HTL, Au contact — quantum‑dot SnO2 gives excellent conformality/low‑T processing and good electron selectivity, consistent with the high‑efficiency SnO2‑based nip cluster.

These five candidates most closely reproduce the composition/ETL/HTL/contact combinations that dominate the top of the training distribution, while lower‑ranked pool candidates (PEDOT:PSS‑based pin devices, exotic/less‑characterized ETL or HTL materials such as TMAH, NDIF2, KY7F22‑np, etc.) are expected to underperform due to poorer band alignment, weaker selectivity, or unproven interface chemistry.

Final: c085, c093, c047, c091, c059
